speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and have noticed a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes. To understand what is causing these symptoms, have you been feeling generally unwell, experiencing fever, or noticing changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acetaminophen Toxicity (Paracetamol Overdose). The combination of agitation, jaundice, and a history of recreational drug use (often associated with non-prescription acetaminophen ingestion) is highly suggestive of liver failure from an overdose, though I will confirm with a liver panel and imaging to rule out other causes like viral hepatitis or cocaine-induced toxicity before finalizing.
